request: if I save £25 a week, when do I reach £500?

beats.intent: Axes of weeks and savings with the line s = 25w
beats.narration: Save twenty five pounds a week and your savings climb in a straight line.
beats.code:
stage.title("Saving up")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 24), y_range=(0, 600), labels=("weeks", "£"))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda w: 25 * w, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: A dashed goal line at £500 meeting the savings line at week 20
beats.narration: The goal is five hundred pounds. The line reaches it at week twenty.
beats.code:
goal = DashedLine(ax.c2p(0, 500), ax.c2p(24, 500), color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(goal))
stage.add(goal)
stage.label(goal, "goal £500", direction=UP, color=YELLOW)
hit = mark_point(stage, ax, (20, 500), color=RED, label="week 20")

beats.narration: Goal divided by weekly saving: five hundred over twenty five is twenty weeks.

request: how do you find the centre of a circle from three points on it?

beats.intent: Three points A, B and C on a faint circle
beats.narration: Here are three points on a circle. Where is its centre?
beats.code:
stage.title("Finding the centre")
c = np.array([0.0, -0.3, 0])
R = 2.2
circle = Circle(radius=R, color=GREY_B, stroke_opacity=0.4).move_to(c)
stage.play(Create(circle))
stage.add(circle)
pts = {n: c + R * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]) for n, a in (("A", 0.3), ("B", 2.0), ("C", 3.9))}
dots = {n: Dot(p, color=YELLOW, radius=0.1) for n, p in pts.items()}
stage.play(*[GrowFromCenter(d) for d in dots.values()])
stage.add(*dots.values())
for n, d in dots.items():
    stage.label(d, n, direction=(d.get_center() - c) / R, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The perpendicular bisector of AB drawn as a long line
beats.narration: Every point equally far from A and B lies on the perpendicular bisector of A B. The centre must be on it.
beats.code:
bis = lambda p, q: Line((p + q) / 2 - 2.8 * np.array([-(q - p)[1], (q - p)[0], 0]) / np.linalg.norm(q - p),
                        (p + q) / 2 + 2.8 * np.array([-(q - p)[1], (q - p)[0], 0]) / np.linalg.norm(q - p), color=BLUE)
ab = Line(pts["A"], pts["B"], color=GREY_B)
b1 = bis(pts["A"], pts["B"])
stage.play(Create(ab), Create(b1))
stage.add(ab, b1)

beats.intent: The bisector of BC crossing it at the centre, marked O
beats.narration: Do the same for B and C. The two bisectors cross at the one point equally far from all three: the centre.
beats.code:
bc = Line(pts["B"], pts["C"], color=GREY_B)
b2 = bis(pts["B"], pts["C"])
b2.set_color(GREEN)
stage.play(Create(bc), Create(b2))
stage.add(bc, b2)
o = Dot(c, color=RED, radius=0.12)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(o))
stage.add(o)
stage.label(o, "O", direction=DR, color=RED)
stage.play(circle.animate.set_stroke(opacity=1, color=WHITE))

request: why do bridges use triangles instead of squares?

beats.intent: A square frame of four bars joined by pins at the corners
beats.narration: Join four bars with pins at the corners to make a square frame.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why triangles?")
sq = Polygon([-4.5, -1.5, 0], [-2.5, -1.5, 0], [-2.5, 0.5, 0], [-4.5, 0.5, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=6)
pins = VGroup(*[Dot(v, color=WHITE, radius=0.1) for v in sq.get_vertices()])
stage.play(Create(sq), FadeIn(pins))
stage.add(sq, pins)

beats.intent: A sideways push squashing the square into a leaning parallelogram
beats.narration: Push it sideways and it folds over: the pins let the angles change, so the square collapses into a leaning shape.
beats.code:
push = Arrow([-6.2, 0.5, 0], [-4.7, 0.5, 0], buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(GrowArrow(push))
stage.add(push)
lean = Polygon([-4.5, -1.5, 0], [-2.5, -1.5, 0], [-1.3, 0.1, 0], [-3.3, 0.1, 0], color=BLUE, stroke_width=6)
stage.play(Transform(sq, lean), *[p.animate.move_to(v) for p, v in zip(pins, lean.get_vertices())])
stage.caption("a square can fold")

beats.intent: A triangle frame beside it that keeps its shape under the same push
beats.narration: Three bars can only meet one way: a triangle's shape is fixed by its side lengths. Push it and it holds, which is why bridges and cranes are made of triangles.
beats.code:
tri = Polygon([1.5, -1.5, 0], [4.0, -1.5, 0], [2.75, 0.7, 0], color=GREEN, stroke_width=6)
tpins = VGroup(*[Dot(v, color=WHITE, radius=0.1) for v in tri.get_vertices()])
stage.play(Create(tri), FadeIn(tpins))
stage.add(tri, tpins)
push2 = Arrow([0.1, 0.7, 0], [1.9, 0.7, 0], buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(GrowArrow(push2))
stage.add(push2)
stage.play(Indicate(tri, color=GREEN))
stage.caption("a triangle holds its shape")

request: what does it mean that a spring stretches in proportion to the force?

beats.intent: A spring hanging from a bar with no weight, its end at 0 cm on a ruler
beats.narration: Hang a spring from a bar. With nothing on it, its end sits at zero.
beats.code:
stage.title("Stretching a spring")
bar = Line([-3, 2.4, 0], [3, 2.4, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=6)
stage.play(Create(bar))
stage.add(bar)
coil = lambda x, L: VMobject(color=WHITE).set_points_as_corners(
    [[x, 2.4, 0]] + [[x + (0.25 if k % 2 else -0.25), 2.4 - (k + 0.5) * L / 12, 0] for k in range(12)] + [[x, 2.4 - L, 0]])
s0 = coil(-2, 1.5)
stage.play(Create(s0))
stage.add(s0)
stage.label(s0, "0 N: 0 cm", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: Two more springs: 2 N stretches 1 cm, 4 N stretches 2 cm, weights hanging
beats.narration: Hang two newtons and it stretches one centimetre more. Four newtons: two centimetres. Double the force, double the stretch.
beats.code:
s1 = coil(0, 2.1)
s2 = coil(2, 2.7)
w1 = Square(0.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7).next_to(s1, DOWN, buff=0)
w2 = Square(0.7, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.7).next_to(s2, DOWN, buff=0)
stage.play(Create(s1), Create(s2), FadeIn(w1), FadeIn(w2))
stage.add(s1, s2, w1, w2)
stage.label(w1, "2 N: 1 cm", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(w2, "4 N: 2 cm", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: Axes of force and stretch with the straight line through (2, 1) and (4, 2)
beats.narration: Plot stretch against force and you get a straight line through zero: this spring stretches half a centimetre per newton.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6), y_range=(0, 3), labels=("N", "cm"))
line = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda f: 0.5 * f, color=GREEN)
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(0, 0), (2, 1), (4, 2)])
stage.caption("stretch = 0.5 cm per newton")
